title.zh: 卷一百八十九 列傳第七十六: 儒學一
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 列傳第七十六: 儒學一 Volume 189 Biographies 76: Confucian Scholars 1

sentences.zh: 列传第七十六 儒学一

translations.literal: Biographies 76: Confucian Scholars, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 76: Confucian Scholars, Part One

sentences.zh: 前代史传，皆以儒学之士，分而为二，以经艺颛门者为儒林，以文章名家者为文苑。

translations.literal: In the historical biographies of earlier dynasties, scholars of Confucian learning were always divided into two categories: those who specialized exclusively in the classics and their arts were placed in the Forest of Scholars, while those famed as masters of literary composition were placed in the Garden of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynastic histories always split Confucian scholars into two groups: specialists in the classics and their arts went into the Forest of Scholars, while those renowned for literary writing went into the Garden of Letters.

sentences.zh: 然儒之为学一也，《六经》者斯道之所在，而文则所以载夫道者也。

translations.literal: Yet the learning of the Ru is one; the Six Classics are where this Way resides, and literature is the means by which that Way is carried.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Confucian learning is fundamentally one: the Six Classics are where the Way itself dwells, and literature is the vehicle that bears it.

sentences.zh: 故经非文则无以发明其旨趣；

translations.literal: Therefore without literature the classics have no means to unfold their purport;
translations.idiomatic: Without literary expression the classics cannot fully unfold their meaning;

sentences.zh: 而文不本于六艺，又乌足谓之文哉。

translations.literal: and literature that is not rooted in the Six Arts—how could it deserve to be called literature?
translations.idiomatic: and writing not grounded in the Six Arts can hardly deserve the name of literature at all.

sentences.zh: 由是而言，经艺文章，不可分而为二也明矣。

translations.literal: From this perspective it is clear that classical learning and literary composition cannot be split into two.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is plain that classical studies and literary art ought never to be treated as two separate things.

sentences.zh: 元兴百年，上自朝廷内外名宦之臣，下及山林布衣之士，以通经能文显著当世者，彬彬焉众矣。

translations.literal: In the century since the rise of the Yuan, from eminent ministers within and without the court above, down to scholars in mountain forests wearing plain cloth below, those who became conspicuous in their age for mastering the classics and excelling in letters have been numerous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the century since the Yuan rose to power, eminent courtiers and humble scholars in the hills alike—anyone distinguished in their day for mastering the classics and writing well—have been legion.

sentences.zh: 今皆不复为之分别，而采取其尤卓然成名、可以辅教传后者，合而隶之，为《儒学传》。

translations.literal: Now we no longer make such a division, but select those especially outstanding in reputation who can aid instruction and be handed down to posterity, gather them together, and assign them to the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: We no longer maintain that split. Instead we gather the most eminent figures whose work can support teaching and endure for posterity into a single Biographies of Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 赵复，字仁甫，德安人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Fu, courtesy name Renfu, was a native of De'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fu, styled Renfu, came from De'an.

sentences.zh: 太宗乙未岁，命太子阔出帅师伐宋，德安以尝逆战，其民数十万，皆俘戮无遗。

translations.literal: In the yimao year of Emperor Taizong, the heir apparent Kuochu was ordered to command an army against Song; because De'an had once resisted in battle, its population of several hundred thousand was taken captive and slaughtered without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year of Taizong's reign the heir apparent Kuochu led an army against Song. Because De'an had once fought back, its population of several hundred thousand was taken captive and wiped out to the last.

sentences.zh: 进杨惟中行中书省军前，姚枢奉诏即军中求儒、道、释、医、卜士，凡儒生挂俘籍者，辄脱之以归，复在其中。

translations.literal: Yang Weizhong advanced to the front of the Central Secretariat army; Yao Shu, by imperial order, sought at once in the army for scholars of Confucianism, Daoism, Buddhism, medicine, and divination. Whenever a Confucian scholar was listed on the captive register, he would release him and send him home; Fu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Weizhong served at the Secretariat army front. Yao Shu, by imperial order, searched the camp for Confucian, Daoist, Buddhist, medical, and divinatory experts. Any Confucian scholar on the captive rolls he freed and sent home; Fu was one of them.

sentences.zh: 枢与之言，信奇士，以九族俱残，不欲北，因与枢诀。

translations.literal: Shu spoke with him and truly found an extraordinary man; because his entire nine degrees of kin had been destroyed, he did not wish to go north, and therefore took leave of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu spoke with him he recognized a man of rare talent. With his entire clan destroyed, Fu refused to go north and took his leave of Shu.

sentences.zh: 枢恐其自裁，留帐中共宿。

translations.literal: Shu feared he would take his own life and kept him in the tent to lodge together.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Fu might kill himself, Shu kept him in the tent and slept there with him.

sentences.zh: 既觉，月色皓然，惟寝衣在，遽驰马周号积尸间，无有也。

translations.literal: When he awoke, the moonlight was bright; only the sleeping garment remained. He immediately galloped his horse, calling out as he circled among the heaped corpses, but Fu was not there.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke the moon was bright and only Fu's sleeping robe remained. Shu galloped off at once, shouting as he searched among the piled corpses, but Fu was gone.

sentences.zh: 行及水际，则见复已被发徒跣，仰天而号，欲投水而未入。

translations.literal: When he reached the water's edge he saw Fu with hair unbound and barefoot, crying to heaven, about to cast himself into the water but not yet having entered.
translations.idiomatic: At the water's edge he found Fu barefoot with hair loose, wailing to heaven, poised to throw himself in but still on the bank.

sentences.zh: 枢晓以徒死无益：「汝存，则子孙或可以传绪百世；

translations.literal: Shu enlightened him that dying in vain would be of no benefit: "If you live, then descendants may perhaps transmit your line for a hundred generations;
translations.idiomatic: Shu reasoned with him that a pointless death would help no one: "If you live, your descendants may yet carry your line forward for generations;

sentences.zh: 随吾而北，必可无他。」

translations.literal: follow me north and you will surely come to no harm."
translations.idiomatic: come north with me and you will surely be safe."

sentences.zh: 复强从之。

translations.literal: Fu reluctantly followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu yielded and went with him.

sentences.zh: 先是，南北道绝，载籍不相通；

translations.literal: Previously the routes between north and south had been cut off and written records did not circulate between them;
translations.idiomatic: Until then the routes between north and south had been severed and books did not pass between them;

sentences.zh: 至是，复以所记程、硃所著诸经传注，尽录以付枢。

translations.literal: at this time Fu copied out in full the commentaries on the classics recorded from memory that had been written by the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi, and gave them all to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: now Fu transcribed from memory the classical commentaries of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi and handed the complete copies to Shu.

sentences.zh: 自复至燕，学子从者百餘人。

translations.literal: From the time Fu arrived in Yan, more than a hundred students followed him to study.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu reached Yan, more than a hundred students came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潜邸，尝召见，问曰：「我欲取宋，卿可导之乎？」

translations.literal: When Shizu was still in his princely residence he once summoned Fu for an audience and asked: "I wish to take Song—could you guide me in doing so?"
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Shizu once summoned Fu and asked, "I intend to conquer Song. Will you guide me?"

sentences.zh: 对曰：「宋，吾父母国也，未有引他人以伐吾父母者。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Song is the country of my parents; there has never been anyone who led others to attack his own parents' country."
translations.idiomatic: Fu answered, "Song is my parents' homeland. No one has ever led outsiders to war against his own parents' country."

sentences.zh: 世祖悦，因不强之仕。

translations.literal: Shizu was pleased and therefore did not press him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was pleased and did not press him to serve.

sentences.zh: 惟中闻复论议，始嗜其学，乃与枢谋建太极书院，立周子祠，以二程、张、杨、游、硃六君子配食，选取遗书八千餘卷，请复讲授其中。

translations.literal: Weizhong, having heard Fu's discourse, came to love his learning; he then joined with Shu in planning to build the Taiji Academy, erect a shrine to Master Zhou, and set out offerings to the six worthies—the two Chengs, Zhang, Yang, You, and Zhu—and selected more than eight thousand volumes of surviving books, inviting Fu to lecture within.
translations.idiomatic: After hearing Fu lecture, Weizhong took up his learning with enthusiasm. He and Shu planned the Taiji Academy, built a shrine to Zhou Dunyi, and installed the two Chengs, Zhang, Yang Shi, You Mao, and Zhu Xi as associated sacrifices. They gathered more than eight thousand volumes of surviving texts and asked Fu to teach there.

sentences.zh: 复以周、程而后，其书广博，学者未能贯通，乃原羲、农、尧、舜所以继天立极，孔子、颜、孟所以垂世立教，周、程、张、硃氏所以发明绍续者，作《传道图》，而以书目条列于后；

translations.literal: Fu, considering that after Zhou Dunyi and the Chengs their books were vast and broad and scholars could not master them through and through, traced back how Fuxi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun succeeded Heaven in establishing the supreme pivot, how Confucius, Yan, and Mencius handed down teaching to the world, and how the Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu schools elucidated and continued the transmission, and composed the Chart of the Transmission of the Way, with a bibliographic list appended afterward;
translations.idiomatic: Finding that post-Zhou and Cheng scholarship had grown so vast that students could not master it whole, Fu traced how Fuxi, Shennong, Yao, and Shun had taken up Heaven's mandate, how Confucius, Yan Hui, and Mencius had handed down teaching to the world, and how Zhou Dunyi, the Chengs, Zhang Zai, and the Zhu school had carried the transmission forward. He composed A Chart of the Transmission of the Way and appended a reading list.

sentences.zh: 别著《伊洛发挥》，以标其宗旨。

translations.literal: He also separately wrote Elucidation of the Yi-Luo tradition to mark its central aim.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Elucidation of the Yi-Luo School to set out its core principles.

sentences.zh: 硃子门人，散在四方，则以见诸登载与得诸传闻者，共五十有三人，作《师友图》，以寓私淑之志。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi's disciples, scattered in the four directions, were gathered—those seen in published records and those known from hearsay—fifty-three in all, and he made the Chart of Teachers and Friends to express his private admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi's disciples were scattered everywhere; Fu collected fifty-three names from published records and reliable report and drew up A Chart of Teachers and Friends to express his private admiration for the tradition.

sentences.zh: 又取伊尹、颜渊言行，作《希贤录》，使学者知所向慕，然后求端用力之方备矣。

translations.literal: He further took the words and conduct of Yi Yin and Yan Yuan and composed the Record of Cherishing the Worthy, so that learners would know what to admire, and thereafter the methods of seeking the root and applying effort would be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on the words and deeds of Yi Yin and Yan Hui, he also wrote A Record of Aspiring to the Worthy so students would know whom to emulate; with that, the path of finding one's footing and applying effort was fully laid out.

sentences.zh: 枢既退隐苏门，乃即复传其学，由是许衡、郝经、刘因，皆得其书而尊信之。

translations.literal: After Shu had retired to seclusion at Sumen, he thereupon transmitted Fu's learning; thereby Xu Heng, Hao Jing, and Liu Yin all obtained his books and honored and trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu retired to Sumen he carried on Fu's teaching. Xu Heng, Hao Jing, and Liu Yin all obtained his writings and held them in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 北方知有程、硃之学，自复始。

translations.literal: That the north came to know the learning of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi began with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The north first learned of Cheng–Zhu learning through Fu.

sentences.zh: 复为人，乐易而耿介，虽居燕，不忘故土。

translations.literal: Fu as a man was easygoing yet upright; though he dwelt in Yan, he did not forget his native land.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was genial yet firm in principle. Though he lived in Yan, he never forgot his homeland.

sentences.zh: 与人交，尤笃分谊。

translations.literal: In dealings with others he was especially devoted to the bonds of moral obligation.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he was especially faithful to the ties of duty and affection.

sentences.zh: 元好问文名擅一时，其南归也，复赠之言，以博溺心、末丧本为戒，以自修读《易》求文王、孔子之用心为勉。

translations.literal: Yuan Haowen's literary fame dominated an age; when he returned south, Fu presented him with words of parting, warning against breadth that drowns the mind and branch learning that loses the root, and urging self-cultivation through reading the Changes to seek the intent of King Wen and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Haowen was the leading literary name of his day. When he went south again, Fu sent him a parting message warning against erudition that floods the mind and specialization that loses the root, and urging him to cultivate himself through the Changes and recover the spirit of King Wen and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 其爱人以德类若此。

translations.literal: His loving others through virtue was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He loved others in this way—always through moral guidance rather than flattery.

sentences.zh: 复家江汉之上，以江汉自号，学者称之曰江汉先生。

translations.literal: Fu's family home was on the Jiang-Han; he took Jiang-Han as his style name, and scholars called him Master Jiang-Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's family had lived along the Jiang and Han rivers, and he styled himself Jiang-Han; scholars called him Master Jiang-Han.

sentences.zh: 张，字达善，其先蜀之导江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, courtesy name Dashan, was by ancestry a native of Daojiang in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, styled Dashan, came from a family originally of Daojiang in Shu.

sentences.zh: 蜀亡，侨寓江左。

translations.literal: When Shu perished, the family sojourned east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell they settled as exiles south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 金华王柏，得硃熹三传之学，尝讲道于台之上蔡书院，从而受业焉。

translations.literal: Wang Bai of Jinhua had received Zhu Xi's learning through three generations of transmission and once expounded the Way at the Shangcai Academy on Mount Tiantai; Yue followed him there to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bai of Jinhua held Zhu Xi's teaching at three removes and once lectured at the Shangcai Academy on Mount Tiantai; Yue studied under him there.

sentences.zh: 自《六经》、《语》、《孟》传注，以及周、程、张氏之微言，硃子所尝论定者，靡不潜心玩索，究极根柢。

translations.literal: From the commentaries on the Six Classics, the Analects, and the Mencius, down to the subtle words of Zhou Dunyi, the Chengs, and Zhang Zai, and whatever Zhu Xi had once adjudicated—there was none he did not study with concentrated devotion, penetrating to the deepest roots.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the commentaries on the Six Classics, the Analects, and Mencius, to the subtle teachings of Zhou Dunyi, the Chengs, and Zhang Zai, and to every point Zhu Xi had settled—working through each to its foundations.

sentences.zh: 用功既专，久而不懈，所学益弘深微密，南北之士，鲜能及之。

translations.literal: His effort being already concentrated and long sustained without slackening, his learning grew ever broader, deeper, subtle, and exact; few scholars north or south could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His study was concentrated and unremitting over many years, until his learning grew vast, deep, and exact. Few scholars anywhere could equal him.

sentences.zh: 至元中，行台中丞吴曼庆闻其名，延致江宁学官，俾子弟受业，中州士大夫欲淑子弟以硃子《四书》者，皆遣从游，或辟私塾迎之。

translations.literal: In the Zhiyuan era, Wu Manqing, Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Regional Secretariat, hearing his name, invited him to Jiangning as a school official so that sons and younger brothers might receive instruction. Central Plain gentry who wished to cultivate their sons and younger brothers in Zhu Xi's Four Books all sent them to study with Yue, or opened private schools to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan reign Wu Manqing, regional vice censor-in-chief, invited him to Jiangning as a school officer so his sons and nephews could study with him. Central Plain families who wanted their sons trained in Zhu Xi's Four Books sent them to Yue or set up private academies to host him.

sentences.zh: 其在维扬，来学者尤众，远近翕然，尊为硕师，不敢字呼，而曰导江先生。

translations.literal: When he was in Weiyang, those who came to study were especially numerous; near and far converged upon him, honoring him as a great master. No one dared call him by his courtesy name, but addressed him as Master Daojiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Weiyang his following was especially large. Students converged from far and near and honored him as a leading master; none would use his courtesy name, calling him only Master Daojiang.

sentences.zh: 大臣荐诸朝，特命为孔、颜、孟三氏教授，邹、鲁之人，服诵遗训，久而不忘。

translations.literal: Great ministers recommended him to the court, and he was specially appointed instructor to the three clans of Confucius, Yan, and Mencius. The people of Zou and Lu recited his transmitted teachings in submission and long did not forget them.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials recommended him to court, and he was specially appointed lecturer to the Kong, Yan, and Meng clans. The people of Zou and Lu received his teaching with reverence and remembered it for years.

sentences.zh: 气宇端重，音吐洪亮，讲说特精详，子弟从之者，诜诜如也。

translations.literal: Yue's bearing was dignified and grave, his voice full and resonant, and his lectures especially precise and thorough; the sons and younger brothers who followed him came in an ever-flowing stream.
translations.idiomatic: Yue bore himself with dignified composure, spoke in a full resonant voice, and lectured with exceptional clarity. The young men who studied under him came in a steady stream.

sentences.zh: 其高第弟子知名者甚多，夹谷之奇、杨刚中尤显。

translations.literal: Among his advanced disciples who became famous there were many; Jiagu Zhiqi and Yang Gangzhong were especially prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his leading disciples became well known, especially Jiagu Zhiqi and Yang Gangzhong.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: Yue had no son.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had no sons.

sentences.zh: 有《经说》及文集行世。

translations.literal: He had Expositions on the Classics and a collected literary works circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Expositions on the Classics and collected writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 吴澄序其书，以为议论正，援据博，贯穿纵横，俨然新安硃氏之尸祝也。

translations.literal: Wu Cheng prefaced his books, considering that his arguments were correct, his citations broad, his penetration comprehensive and free-ranging—truly like the sacrificial officiant of the Zhu clan of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng wrote a preface to his works, praising their sound reasoning, wide citation, and comprehensive grasp—declaring him a true heir to the Zhu school of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 至正中，真州守臣以及郝经、吴澄皆尝留仪真，作祠宇祀之，曰三贤祠。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era the prefectural officials of Zhenzhou, because Yue together with Hao Jing and Wu Cheng had all once stayed at Yizhen, built a shrine to sacrifice to them, called the Shrine of the Three Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era the magistrates of Zhen prefecture, noting that Yue, Hao Jing, and Wu Cheng had all once lived at Yizhen, built a shrine to honor the three and called it the Shrine of the Three Worthies.

sentences.zh: 金履祥，字吉父，婺之兰溪人。

translations.literal: Jin Lüxiang, courtesy name Jifu, was a native of Lanxi in Wu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Lüxiang, styled Jifu, came from Lanxi in Wu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先本刘氏，后避吴越钱武肃王嫌名，更为金氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors had originally been of the Liu clan; later, to avoid the tabooed name of Qian Liu, King Wusu of Wuyue, they changed to the Jin clan.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been surnamed Liu; later, to avoid the taboo name of Wuyue's King Wusu, Qian Liu, they adopted the surname Jin.

sentences.zh: 履祥从曾祖景文，当宋建炎、绍兴间，以孝行著称，其父母疾，斋祷于天，而灵应随至。

translations.literal: Lüxiang's great-uncle Jingwen, during the Jianyan and Shaoxing reigns of Song, was famed for filial conduct; when his parents fell ill he fasted and prayed to Heaven, and spiritual responses followed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxiang's great-uncle Jingwen, in the Jianyan and Shaoxing eras of Song, was renowned for filial piety. When his parents fell ill he fasted and prayed to Heaven, and miraculous responses came at once.

sentences.zh: 事闻于朝，为改所居乡曰纯孝。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the court, his home township was renamed Pure Filiality.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of it, his home township was renamed Pure Filiality.

sentences.zh: 履祥幼而敏睿，父兄稍授之书，即能记诵。

translations.literal: Lüxiang in youth was keen and intelligent; when father and elder brothers gave him even a little instruction in books, he could at once memorize and recite.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxiang was clever as a boy; whatever his father and elder brothers taught him from books he could memorize at once.

sentences.zh: 比长，益自策励，凡天文、地形、礼乐、田乘、兵谋、阴阳、律历之书，靡不毕究。

translations.literal: When he grew older he urged himself on still more; every book on astronomy, topography, ritual and music, agriculture and transport, military strategy, yin-yang, and calendrical calculation—there was none he did not thoroughly investigate.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he drove himself harder still, mastering every field from astronomy and geography to ritual, agriculture, military strategy, yin-yang theory, and calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 及壮，知向濂、洛之学，事同郡王柏，从登何基之门。

translations.literal: When he reached maturity he turned toward the learning of the Lian and Luo schools, served Wang Bai of the same commandery, and through him entered the gate of He Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In adulthood he turned to the Lian–Luo tradition, studied under Wang Bai of his own prefecture, and through him entered He Ji's school.

sentences.zh: 基则学于黄ＯＥ，而ＯＥ亲承硃熹之传者也。

translations.literal: Ji had studied under Huang Gan, and Gan had personally received Zhu Xi's transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had studied under Huang Gan, who had received Zhu Xi's teaching directly.

sentences.zh: 自是讲贯益密，造诣益邃。

translations.literal: From this time his lecturing and practice grew ever more exact, and his attainment ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his study grew ever more rigorous and his attainment ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 时宋之国事已不可为，履祥遂绝意进取。

translations.literal: At that time Song's national affairs were already beyond remedy, and Lüxiang therefore utterly abandoned any thought of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: By then Song's state was beyond saving, and Lüxiang gave up all thought of official advancement.

sentences.zh: 然负其经济之略，亦未忍遽忘斯世也。

translations.literal: Yet bearing within him strategies for ordering the state, he could not yet bear abruptly to forget this world.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still carried plans for ordering the state and could not bring himself to turn his back on the world.

sentences.zh: 会襄樊之师日急，宋人坐视而不敢救，履祥因进牵制捣虚之策，请以重兵由海道直趋燕、蓟，则襄樊之师，将不攻而自解。

translations.literal: It happened that the armies at Xiang and Fan grew daily more pressing, while the Song sat watching and dared not rescue them; Lüxiang therefore submitted a strategy of checking the enemy and striking at emptiness, proposing that heavy forces be sent by sea route straight toward Yan and Ji—then the armies at Xiang and Fan would dissolve without being attacked.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng grew desperate and Song forces dared not relieve it, Lüxiang proposed a diversion: send a strong fleet by sea straight at Yan and Ji, and the Xiang–Fan armies would collapse without a direct assault.

sentences.zh: 且备叙海舶所经，凡州郡县邑，下至巨洋别坞，难易远近，历历可据以行。

translations.literal: Moreover he fully described the route of sea vessels, every prefecture, commandery, county, and district, down to great seas and separate harbors, their difficulty, ease, distance, and nearness—each itemized so that one could navigate by it.
translations.idiomatic: He also mapped the sea route in detail—every prefecture, county, and harbor, every stretch of open ocean, with distances and difficulties noted so clearly that a fleet could follow his chart.

sentences.zh: 宋终莫能用。

translations.literal: Song in the end never employed it.
translations.idiomatic: Song never adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 及后硃瑄、张清献海运之利，而所由海道，视履祥先所上书，咫尺无异者，然后人服其精确。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhu Xuan and Zhang Qingxian demonstrated the profit of transport by sea, the sea route they used differed from what Lüxiang had earlier submitted in his memorial by scarcely a foot or an inch; only then did later men acknowledge his precision.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhu Xuan and Zhang Qingxian proved the value of sea transport, the route they used matched Lüxiang's earlier memorial almost point for point, and posterity marveled at his accuracy.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，以迪功郎、史馆编校起之，辞弗就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deyou era he was summoned as Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement and collator in the Historiography Institute, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Deyou era he was summoned as a junior merit officer and historiography collator, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 宋将改物，所在盗起，履祥屏居金华山中，兵燹稍息，则上下岩谷，追逐云月，寄情啸咏，视世故泊如也。

translations.literal: As Song was about to change its mandate, bandits rose everywhere; Lüxiang withdrew to seclusion in the Jinhua mountains. When the flames of war subsided somewhat, he would ascend and descend the rocky valleys, pursuing clouds and moon, placing his feelings in chanting and song, viewing worldly affairs as tranquil indeed.
translations.idiomatic: As the Song dynasty neared its end, banditry spread everywhere. Lüxiang withdrew to the Jinhua mountains. When fighting eased he wandered the peaks, chasing moonlight and clouds, finding solace in poetry, and treating worldly affairs with complete detachment.

sentences.zh: 平居独处，终日俨然；

translations.literal: In ordinary life, dwelling alone, he was dignified all day long;
translations.idiomatic: In daily life, when alone, he maintained a dignified bearing throughout the day;

sentences.zh: 至与物接，则盎然和怿。

translations.literal: yet when he came into contact with things, he was fully harmonious and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: yet in company he was warm and entirely at ease.

sentences.zh: 训迪后学，谆切无倦，而尤笃于分义。

translations.literal: In instructing and guiding later learners he was earnest and tireless, and especially devoted to the bonds of moral obligation.
translations.idiomatic: He taught younger scholars with tireless earnestness and was especially faithful to the bonds of duty and friendship.

sentences.zh: 有故人子坐事，母子分配为隶，不相知者十年，履祥倾赀营购，卒赎以完；

translations.literal: There was the son of an old acquaintance who was implicated in a case; mother and son were assigned as bondsmen to different places and did not know each other's whereabouts for ten years. Lüxiang exhausted his resources to arrange purchase and in the end ransomed them so they were made whole;
translations.idiomatic: An old friend's son was implicated in a case and mother and son were sold into bondage in separate places, ignorant of each other's fate for ten years. Lüxiang spent his entire means to buy their freedom and reunited them;

sentences.zh: 其子后贵，履祥终不自言，相见劳问辛苦而已。

translations.literal: when the son later rose to eminence, Lüxiang to the end never spoke of it himself; when they met he merely inquired after his hardships.
translations.idiomatic: when the son later rose to high rank Lüxiang never mentioned what he had done; when they met he only asked after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 何基、王柏之丧，履祥率其同门之士，以义制服，观者始知师弟子之系于常伦也。

translations.literal: At the funerals of He Ji and Wang Bai, Lüxiang led his fellow disciples in wearing mourning according to the rites of righteousness; observers for the first time understood how teacher and disciples are bound to ordinary human relations.
translations.idiomatic: At the funerals of He Ji and Wang Bai, Lüxiang led his fellow disciples in proper mourning dress, and onlookers saw for the first time how deeply the bond between teacher and pupil belongs to ordinary human duty.

sentences.zh: 履祥尝谓司马文正公光作《资治通鉴》，秘书丞刘恕为《外纪》，以记前事，不本于经，而信百家之说，是非谬于圣人，不足以传信。

translations.literal: Lüxiang once said that when the Cultivated Duke of State, Sima Guang, composed the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, the Secretariat Assistant Liu Shu made an Outer Annals to record earlier events; not basing himself on the classics but trusting the sayings of the hundred schools, right and wrong diverged from the sages and were insufficient to transmit credibly.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxiang once observed that when Sima Guang wrote the Comprehensive Mirror, Liu Shu compiled an Outer Annals for earlier ages. Because it relied on the hundred schools rather than the classics, its judgments diverged from the sages and could not be trusted as reliable history.

sentences.zh: 自帝尧以前，不经夫子所定，固野而难质。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Yao, what had not been fixed by the Master was of course uncouth and hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Events before Emperor Yao, not fixed by the Master's hand, are necessarily crude and hard to verify.

sentences.zh: 夫子因鲁史以作《春秋》，王朝列国之事，非有玉帛之使，则鲁史不得而书，非圣人笔削之所加也。

translations.literal: The Master took the Lu chronicle to compose the Spring and Autumn; affairs of the royal court and the feudal states—unless there were envoys bearing jade and silk, the Lu chronicle could not record them, and they were not matters upon which the sage's editing brush fell.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius drew on the Lu chronicle to compose the Spring and Autumn. Affairs of the royal house and the states could enter it only when Lu had diplomatic contact; much else lay outside the sage's editorial judgment.

sentences.zh: 况左氏所记，或阙或诬，凡此类皆不得以辟经为辞。

translations.literal: Moreover what Zuo Qiuming recorded is sometimes deficient and sometimes false; all such matters cannot be excused on the plea of supplementing the classic.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zuo Qiuming's record is sometimes incomplete and sometimes false; none of this may be justified as supplementing the classic.

sentences.zh: 乃用邵氏《皇极经世历》、胡氏《皇王大纪》之例，损益折衷，一以《尚书》为主，下及《诗》、《礼》、《春秋》，旁采旧史诸子，表年系事，断自唐尧以下，接于《通鉴》之前，勒为一书，二十卷，名曰《通鉴前编》。

translations.literal: He therefore adopted the models of Shao Yong's Supreme Pivot Chronology and Hu Hong's Annals of Emperors and Kings, adding and subtracting in balanced compromise, taking the Documents as primary, extending down to the Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn, and collaterally drawing on old histories and the various masters; he tabulated years and linked events, beginning from below Emperor Yao and joining what comes before the Comprehensive Mirror, and carved it into one book of twenty scrolls, entitled Precedents to the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Following the models of Shao Yong's Supreme Pivot Chronology and Hu Hong's Annals of Emperors and Kings, he weighed and harmonized their methods, took the Documents as his foundation, drew on the Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn, and supplemented them from older histories and the masters. He tabulated years and linked events from the age of Yao down to where the Comprehensive Mirror begins, and compiled twenty scrolls entitled Precedents to the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 凡所引书，辄加训释，以裁正其义，多儒先所未发。

translations.literal: For every book he cited he added exegesis to adjudicate and correct its meaning; much of it had not been brought forth by earlier Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Every text he cited he glossed to settle its meaning, often articulating points earlier Confucians had never raised.

sentences.zh: 既成，以授门人许谦曰：「二帝三王之盛，其微言懿行，宜后王所当法，战国申、商之术，其苛法乱政，亦后王所当戒，则是编不可以不著也。」

translations.literal: When it was finished he gave it to his disciple Xu Qian, saying: "In the splendor of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, their subtle words and excellent conduct ought to be what later kings take as models; the techniques of Shenzi and Shang Yang in the Warring States period, with their harsh laws and disordering government, are also what later kings ought to take as warnings—therefore this compilation cannot fail to be published."
translations.idiomatic: When it was done he handed it to Xu Qian, saying, "The subtle words and noble conduct of the Two Emperors and Three Kings are what later rulers should emulate; the harsh legalism of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang in the Warring States is what they should shun. This work therefore must not be left unpublished."

sentences.zh: 他所著书，曰《大学章句疏义》二卷，《论语孟子集注考证》十七卷，《书表注》四卷，谦为益加校定，皆传于学者。

translations.literal: His other books included: Expository Meaning of the Great Learning Chapter and Sentences, two scrolls; Textual Verification of the Collected Commentaries on the Analects and Mencius, seventeen scrolls; Tabular Commentary on the Documents, four scrolls—Qian further collated and corrected them, and all were transmitted among scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His other works included Expository Meaning of the Great Learning (two scrolls), Textual Verification of the Collected Commentaries on the Analects and Mencius (seventeen scrolls), and Tabular Commentary on the Documents (four scrolls). Qian revised them further, and all circulated among scholars.

sentences.zh: 天历初，廉访使郑允中表上其书于朝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianli era the surveillance commissioner Zheng Yunzhong memorialized his books to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli era surveillance commissioner Zheng Yunzhong presented his works to court.

sentences.zh: 初，履祥既见王柏，首问为学之方，柏告以必先立志，且举先儒之言：居敬以持其志，立志以定其本，志立乎事物之表，敬行乎事物之内，此为学之大方也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lüxiang had first met Wang Bai, he asked above all for the method of learning; Bai told him he must first establish his will, and cited words of earlier Confucians: "Maintain reverence to hold your will; establish your will to fix your root. The will is established beyond things and affairs; reverence is practiced within things and affairs"—this is the great method of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Lüxiang first met Wang Bai he asked how to study. Bai told him to establish his will first and quoted earlier masters: "Maintain reverence to sustain your will; establish your will to fix your foundation. Will stands above affairs; reverence operates within them"—that, he said, is the great principle of learning.

sentences.zh: 及见何基，基谓之曰：「会之屡言贤者之贤，理欲之分，便当自今始。」

translations.literal: When he met He Ji, Ji said to him: "Huizhi has often spoken of the worthiness of the worthy and the division between principle and desire—you ought to begin from today."
translations.idiomatic: When he met He Ji, Ji told him, "Huizhi has often spoken of what makes the worthy worthy and of the divide between principle and desire. Take that as your starting point from today."

sentences.zh: 会之，盖柏字也。

translations.literal: Huizhi was Wang Bai's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi was Wang Bai's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 当时议者以为基之清介纯实似尹和静，柏之高明刚正似谢上蔡，履祥则亲得之二氏，而并充于己者也。

translations.literal: Contemporary commentators considered that Ji's purity, integrity, and genuineness resembled Yin Hejing, Bai's loftiness, clarity, firmness, and rectitude resembled Xie Shangcai, while Lüxiang had personally obtained both men's teaching and fully embodied them in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said Ji's purity and integrity recalled Yin Hejing, Bai's loftiness and firm rectitude recalled Xie Shangcai, and Lüxiang had received both traditions directly and made them fully his own.

sentences.zh: 履祥居仁山之下，学者因称为仁山先生。

translations.literal: Lüxiang dwelt below Mount Ren; scholars therefore called him Master Renshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxiang lived below Mount Ren, and scholars called him Master Renshan.

sentences.zh: 大德中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Dade era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dade era.

sentences.zh: 元统初，里人吴师道为国子博士，移书学官，祠履祥于乡学。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuantong era his townsman Wu Shidao, a doctor of the National University, sent a letter to the school officials to sacrifice to Lüxiang at the district academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuantong era his townsman Wu Shidao, then a National University lecturer, wrote to the local school authorities asking that Lüxiang be honored at the district academy.

sentences.zh: 至正中，赐谥文安。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng era he was granted the posthumous title Cultivated Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era he was granted the posthumous title Cultivated Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 许谦，字益之，其先京兆人。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, courtesy name Yizhi, was by ancestry a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, styled Yizhi, came from a family originally of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 九世祖延寿，宋刑部尚书。

translations.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Yan Shou was Minister of Justice of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His ninth-generation ancestor Yan Shou served Song as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 八世祖仲容，太子洗马。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhongrong was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stables.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhongrong was groom of the heir apparent's stables.

sentences.zh: 仲容之子曰洸、曰洞，洞由进士起家，以文章政事知名于时。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's sons were named Guang and Dong; Dong rose through the jinshi examination and was famed in his time for literary composition and governmental affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong had two sons, Guang and Dong. Dong entered office through the jinshi examination and was renowned for both literary talent and administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 洸之子寔，事海陵胡瑗，能以师法终始者也。

translations.literal: Guang's son Shi studied under Hu Yuan of Hailing and was one who could carry the master's method through from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son Shi studied under Hu Yuan of Hailing and carried his teacher's method through to the end.

sentences.zh: 由平江徙婺之金华，至谦五世，为金华人。

translations.literal: The family moved from Pingjiang to Jinhua in Wu; by Qian's time, five generations on, they were natives of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: The family moved from Pingjiang to Jinhua in Wu prefecture; five generations later Qian was a native of Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 父觥，登淳祐七年进士第，仕未显以殁。

translations.literal: His father Gong passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Chunyou but died before his service became conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong passed the jinshi in the seventh year of Chunyou but died before achieving notable office.

sentences.zh: 谦生数岁而孤，甫能言，世母陶氏口授《孝经》、《论语》，入耳辄不忘。

translations.literal: Qian was orphaned at a few years of age; as soon as he could speak, his step-grandmother Lady Tao orally taught him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, and what entered his ears he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Qian lost his father when he was only a few years old. As soon as he could speak his step-grandmother Lady Tao taught him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects by heart, and he never forgot a word.

sentences.zh: 稍长，肆力于学，立程以自课，取四部书分昼夜读之，虽疾恙不废。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older he threw his strength into learning, set a schedule to examine himself, took the books of the four divisions and divided them between day and night for reading, and did not stop even when ill.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he threw himself into study, set himself a daily schedule, and divided the four bibliographic divisions between day and night reading—even illness did not interrupt him.

sentences.zh: 既乃受业金履祥之门，履祥语之曰：「士之为学，若五味之在和，醯酱既加，则酸鹹顿异。

translations.literal: Thereafter he received instruction at Jin Lüxiang's gate; Lüxiang said to him: "When a scholar pursues learning it is like the blending of the five flavors—once vinegar and sauce are added, sour and salty are instantly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He then studied under Jin Lüxiang, who told him, "A scholar's learning is like blending the five flavors: add vinegar or sauce and sour and salty change at once.

sentences.zh: 子来见我已三日，而犹夫人也，岂吾之学无以感发子耶！」

translations.literal: You have come to see me for three days, yet you are still the same as before—can it be that my learning has no power to move and awaken you!"
translations.idiomatic: You have studied with me for three days and are still unchanged. Can it be that my teaching has failed to move you at all?"

sentences.zh: 谦闻之惕然。

translations.literal: When Qian heard this he was startled into vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Qian took the rebuke to heart and redoubled his vigilance.

sentences.zh: 居数年，尽得其所传之奥。

translations.literal: After several years he fully obtained the profundities of what had been transmitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had mastered the deepest teachings of his master.

sentences.zh: 于书无不读，穷探圣微，虽残文羡语，皆不敢忽。

translations.literal: There was no book he did not read; he exhaustively probed the subtlety of the sages, and even fragmentary texts and surplus phrases he dared not neglect.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and probed the sages' subtlest meanings; even fragmentary passages and stray lines he refused to dismiss lightly.

sentences.zh: 有不可通，则不敢强；

translations.literal: what could not be made to cohere, he did not dare force;
translations.idiomatic: Where meaning would not cohere he refused to force an interpretation;

sentences.zh: 于先儒之说，有所未安，亦不苟同也。

translations.literal: in the sayings of earlier Confucians, where he was not at ease, he likewise did not agree without reflection.
translations.idiomatic: and where earlier Confucians left him unconvinced he would not agree merely out of deference.

sentences.zh: 又有《自省编》，昼之所为，夜必书之，其不可书者，则不为也。

translations.literal: He also had the Self-Examination Record: what he did by day he was sure to write at night; what could not be written, he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept a Self-Examination Record: each night he wrote down the day's conduct, and what he could not bear to record he refused to do.

sentences.zh: 其他若天文、地理、典章、制度、食货、刑法、字学、音韵、医经、术数之说，亦靡不该贯，旁而释、老之言，亦洞究其蕴。

translations.literal: As for other fields—astronomy, geography, statutes and regulations, institutions, food and goods, penal law, philology, phonology, medical classics, and numerological arts—there was none he did not master comprehensively; even on the side, Buddhist and Daoist writings he also penetrated to their inner meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He was equally versed in astronomy, geography, ritual codes, institutions, economics, penal law, philology, phonology, medicine, and numerology; he even penetrated deeply into Buddhist and Daoist writings.

sentences.zh: 尝谓：「学者孰不曰辟异端，苟不深探其隐，而识其所以然，能辨其同异，别其是非也几希。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Which scholar does not say he repudiates heterodox teachings? Yet if one does not deeply probe their hidden aspects and understand their reasons for being so, one who can distinguish their sameness and difference and separate their right and wrong is exceedingly rare."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Every scholar claims to reject heterodox teachings, but without probing their hidden logic and grasping why they arose, few can truly distinguish agreement from difference or right from wrong."

sentences.zh: 又尝句读《九经》、《仪礼》及《春秋三传》，于其宏纲要领，错简衍文，悉别以铅黄硃墨，意有所明，则表而见之。

translations.literal: He also once punctuated and sectioned the Nine Classics, the Rites of Zhou, and the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn; for their great outlines and essential points, misplaced bamboo slips and interpolated passages, he distinguished all with lead, yellow, cinnabar, and ink, and where his meaning was clarified he set it forth in tables.
translations.idiomatic: He also punctuated the Nine Classics, the Rites, and the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, marking main themes, corruptions, and interpolations in colored ink and tabulating every clarification.

sentences.zh: 其后吴师道购得吕祖谦点校《仪礼》，视谦所定，不同者十有三条而已。

translations.literal: Later Wu Shidao purchased Lü Zuqian's collated Rites of Zhou and, comparing it with Qian's determinations, found only thirteen points of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Shidao obtained Lü Zuqian's collated Rites and found only thirteen points of disagreement with Qian's text.

sentences.zh: 谦不喜矜露，所为诗文，非扶翼经义，张维世教，则未尝轻笔之书也。

translations.literal: Qian did not like to display himself; the poetry and prose he wrote, unless they supported the classics' meaning or upheld worldly teaching, he never lightly put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: Qian disliked self-display and never wrote poetry or prose unless it supported the classics or upheld public morals.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，谦居东阳八华山，学者翕然从之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou era Qian dwelt on Mount Bajua in Dongyang, and scholars converged upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanyou era Qian lived on Mount Bajua in Dongyang, and students flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 寻开门讲学，远而幽、冀、齐、鲁，近而荆、扬、吴、越，皆不惮百舍来受业焉。

translations.literal: Soon he opened his doors to lecture; from afar You, Ji, Qi, and Lu, and from near Jing, Yang, Wu, and Yue—all did not shrink from traveling a hundred lodges to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon opened his school to the public. Students from as far as You, Ji, Qi, and Lu and as near as Jing, Yang, Wu, and Yue traveled a hundred leagues without hesitation to study with him.

sentences.zh: 其教人也，至诚谆悉，内外殚尽，尝曰：「己有知，使人亦知之，岂不快哉！」

translations.literal: In teaching others he was utterly sincere, earnest, and thorough, exhausting himself inwardly and outwardly. He once said: "When I have knowledge and enable others to know it too, is that not a joy!"
translations.idiomatic: He taught with complete sincerity and tireless care, giving all he had within and without. He once said, "When I know something and can help another know it too, what greater joy is there?"

sentences.zh: 或有所问难，而词不能自达，则为之言其所欲言，而解其所惑。

translations.literal: When someone raised a difficulty but could not express himself in words, Qian would speak for him what he wished to say and resolve what puzzled him.
translations.idiomatic: When a student could not frame a question clearly, Qian would put the question into words for him and resolve his confusion.

sentences.zh: 讨论讲贯，终日不倦，摄其粗疏，入于密微。

translations.literal: In discussion and lecturing he was tireless all day, drawing what was coarse and loose into what was subtle and exact.
translations.idiomatic: In discussion he never tired, drawing students from rough understanding into subtle mastery.

sentences.zh: 闻者方倾耳听受，而其出愈真切。

translations.literal: Just as listeners were inclining their ears to receive his teaching, his utterances grew ever more genuine and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Just as listeners leaned in to hear him, his words grew ever more direct and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 惰者作之，锐者抑之，拘者开之，放者约之。

translations.literal: The indolent he roused; the over-sharp he restrained; the constrained he opened; the unrestrained he brought to measure.
translations.idiomatic: He roused the lazy, checked the overbold, opened the narrow-minded, and restrained the reckless.

sentences.zh: 及门之士，著录者千餘人，随其材分，咸有所得。

translations.literal: Disciples at his gate, more than a thousand on the register, each according to his talent and allotment, all gained something.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand students enrolled at his school, and each, according to his gifts, gained something real.

sentences.zh: 然独不以科举之文授人，曰：「此义、利之所由分也。」

translations.literal: Yet he alone did not teach others examination essays, saying: "This is where righteousness and profit divide."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he alone refused to teach examination essays, saying, "This is where righteousness and profit part ways."

sentences.zh: 谦笃于孝友，有绝人之行。

translations.literal: Qian was devoted to filial piety and brotherly affection and had conduct surpassing ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was deeply devoted to family duty and possessed conduct that set him apart from ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 其处世不胶于古，不流于俗。

translations.literal: In dealing with the world he was neither glued to antiquity nor swept along by fashion.
translations.idiomatic: In worldly affairs he was neither rigidly antiquarian nor swept along by fashion.

sentences.zh: 不出里闾者四十年，四方之士，以不及门为耻，缙绅先生之过其乡邦者，必即其家存问焉。

translations.literal: For forty years he did not leave his village lanes; scholars from the four directions took it as shame not to have entered his gate, and gentry and elders passing through his district were sure to call at his home to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years he never left his home district. Scholars from every quarter regarded failure to study with him as a disgrace, and officials passing through always called at his door.

sentences.zh: 或访以典礼政事，谦观其会通，而为之折衷，闻者无不厌服。

translations.literal: When consulted on ritual and governmental affairs, Qian observed their points of convergence and made balanced judgments for them; listeners were without exception fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When asked about ritual or policy he weighed the issues comprehensively and offered balanced judgments that left every listener convinced.

sentences.zh: 大德中，荧惑入南斗句已而行，谦以为灾在吴、楚，窃深忧之。

translations.literal: In the Dade era Mars entered the Southern Dipper, lingered a brief period, and departed; Qian considered that disaster would fall on Wu and Chu and privately was deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era Mars entered the Southern Dipper, paused briefly, and moved on. Qian feared disaster for Wu and Chu and grieved in private.

sentences.zh: 是岁大昆，谦貌加瘠，或问曰：「岂食不足邪？」

translations.literal: That year there was a great famine; Qian's appearance grew still more emaciated. Someone asked: "Is it perhaps that food is insufficient?"
translations.idiomatic: That year famine struck and Qian grew visibly thinner. Someone asked, "Are you going hungry?"

sentences.zh: 谦曰：「今公私匮竭，道殣相望，吾能独饱邪！」

translations.literal: Qian said: "Now public and private stores are exhausted and corpses of the starved line the roads—how could I eat my fill alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied, "Public and private stores are empty and the starving lie along every road. How can I eat my fill alone?"

sentences.zh: 其处心盖如此。

translations.literal: His disposition of heart was generally of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His heart was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 廉访使刘庭直、副使赵宏伟，皆中州雅望，于谦深加推服，论荐于朝；

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioners Liu Tingzhi and Vice Commissioner Zhao Hongwei were both men of refined reputation in the Central Plain; Qian deeply admired and submitted to them and discussed recommending them to court;
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Liu Tingzhi and vice commissioner Zhao Hongwei were both men of high standing in the Central Plain. Qian admired them deeply and urged their recommendation to court;

sentences.zh: 中外名臣列其行义者，前后章数十上；

translations.literal: famous ministers within and without the court memorialized listing his conduct and righteousness, dozens of memorials in succession;
translations.idiomatic: distinguished officials at court and in the provinces submitted dozens of memorials praising his conduct;

sentences.zh: 而郡复以遗逸应诏；

translations.literal: and the commandery again nominated him as a reclusive worthy in response to an edict;
translations.idiomatic: the prefecture repeatedly nominated him as a reclusive worthy in response to imperial edicts;

sentences.zh: 乡闱大比，请司其文衡。

translations.literal: at the great provincial examinations they requested him to preside over the literary scales—
translations.idiomatic: at major provincial examinations they asked him to serve as chief examiner—

sentences.zh: 皆莫能致。

translations.literal: yet none could bring him forth.
translations.idiomatic: yet none could secure his acceptance.

sentences.zh: 至其晚节，独以身任正学之重，远近学者，以其身之安否，为斯道之隆替焉。

translations.literal: In his later years he alone bore on his person the weight of orthodox learning; scholars near and far took whether his person was safe or in peril as the rise or decline of this Way.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he alone bore the weight of orthodox learning on his shoulders. Scholars everywhere treated his well-being as the barometer of the tradition's fortunes.

sentences.zh: 至元三年卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Zhiyuan at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 尝以白云山人自号，世称为白云先生。

translations.literal: He once styled himself the Mountain Man of White Clouds; the world called him Master White Cloud.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself the Mountain Man of White Clouds, and the world called him Master White Cloud.

sentences.zh: 朝廷赐谥文懿。

translations.literal: The court granted the posthumous title Cultivated and Virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the posthumous title Cultivated and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 先是，何基、王柏及金履祥殁，其学犹未大显，至谦而其道益著，故学者推原统绪，以为硃熹之世適。

translations.literal: Earlier, after He Ji, Wang Bai, and Jin Lüxiang had died, their learning had not yet become greatly manifest; with Qian their Way grew still more prominent, and therefore scholars traced back the lineage of transmission and considered him the true successor of Zhu Xi's age.
translations.idiomatic: After He Ji, Wang Bai, and Jin Lüxiang died their teaching had not yet fully flourished. Under Qian it became conspicuous, and scholars traced the lineage back to declare him Zhu Xi's true heir in their generation.

sentences.zh: 江浙行中书省为请于朝，建四贤书院，以奉祠事，而列于学官。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Regional Secretariat requested of the court permission to build the Academy of the Four Worthies to maintain sacrificial services, and listed them among the school officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe regional secretariat petitioned court to build the Academy of the Four Worthies for their cult and enrolled them among the official school sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 同郡硃震亨，字彦修，谦之高第弟子也。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhenheng of the same commandery, courtesy name Yanxiu, was Qian's advanced disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhenheng of the same prefecture, styled Yanxiu, was one of Qian's leading disciples.

sentences.zh: 其清修苦节，绝类古笃行之士，所至人多化之。

translations.literal: His pure cultivation and bitter integrity closely resembled the earnestly practicing men of antiquity; wherever he went many were transformed by him.
translations.idiomatic: His austere integrity recalled the earnest practitioners of antiquity, and wherever he went he transformed those around him.

sentences.zh: 陈栎，字寿翁，徽之休宁人。

translations.literal: Chen Li, courtesy name Shouweng, was a native of Xiuning in Hu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Li, styled Shouweng, came from Xiuning in Hu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 栎生三岁，祖母吴氏口授《孝经》、《论语》，辄成诵。

translations.literal: Li at three years of age had his grandmother Lady Wu orally teach him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, and he could at once recite them.
translations.idiomatic: At three Li's grandmother Lady Wu taught him the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects by heart, and he could recite them immediately.

sentences.zh: 五岁入小学，即涉猎经史。

translations.literal: At five he entered elementary study and at once ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: At five he began formal schooling and was already reading widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 七岁通进士业。

translations.literal: At seven he mastered the curriculum for the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: By seven he had mastered the jinshi examination curriculum.

sentences.zh: 十五，乡人皆师之。

translations.literal: At fifteen the people of his district all took him as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen his neighbors all looked to him as their teacher.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，科举废，栎慨然发愤，致力于圣人之学，涵濡玩索，贯穿古今。

translations.literal: When Song perished and the examinations were abolished, Li indignantly roused his spirit and devoted himself to the learning of the sages, soaking and savoring it, threading it through past and present.
translations.idiomatic: When Song fell and the examinations ended, Li threw himself into the sages' learning with passionate resolve, immersing himself in it until it ran through past and present alike.

sentences.zh: 尝以谓有功于圣门者，莫若硃熹氏，熹没未久，而诸家之说，往往乱其本真，乃著《四书发明》、《书集传纂疏》、《礼记集义》等书，亡虑数十万言，凡诸儒之说，有畔于硃氏者，刊而去之；

translations.literal: He once said that among those who had rendered service to the sage's gate, none surpassed the Zhu clan; not long after Xi's death the various schools' doctrines often confused his authentic teaching. He therefore composed such books as Elucidation of the Four Books, Collated Commentary on the Collected Commentaries on the Documents, and Collected Meanings of the Book of Rites—altogether no less than several hundred thousand words. Whatever sayings of the various Confucians deviated from the Zhu school, he excised and removed them;
translations.idiomatic: He held that no one since the sage's school had served it better than Zhu Xi, yet soon after Xi's death rival schools had blurred his teaching. Li therefore wrote Elucidation of the Four Books, Collated Commentary on the Documents, Collected Meanings of the Book of Rites, and other works totaling hundreds of thousands of words, cutting away every interpretation that deviated from Zhu Xi;

sentences.zh: 其微辞隐义，则引而伸之；

translations.literal: their subtle words and hidden meanings he drew forth and extended;
translations.idiomatic: where Zhu's subtle meanings were compressed he drew them out and extended them;

sentences.zh: 而其所未备者，复为说以补其阙。

translations.literal: and where Zhu had not yet been complete, he again composed explanations to fill the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: and where Zhu had left gaps he supplied explanations of his own.

sentences.zh: 于是硃熹之说大明于世。

translations.literal: Thus Zhu Xi's doctrines became greatly illuminated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhu Xi's teaching shone brightly throughout the world.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，诏以科举取士，栎不欲就试，有司强之，试乡闱中选，遂不复赴礼部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanyou era an edict ordered selection of scholars through the examinations; Li did not wish to take the test, but the authorities compelled him. He passed the provincial examination but never again went to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanyou era the court restored the examinations. Li did not wish to compete, but officials forced him. He passed the provincial examination and never went on to the capital examination.

sentences.zh: 教授于家，不出门户者数十年。

translations.literal: He taught at home and for decades did not pass beyond his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at home and did not leave his gate for decades.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，尤刚正，日用之间，动中礼法。

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, especially upright and firm, in daily use his every movement hit the mark of ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial and upright, and in daily life his every act accorded with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 与人交，不以势合，不以利迁。

translations.literal: In dealings with others he did not associate because of power, nor shift because of profit.
translations.idiomatic: In friendship he neither courted the powerful nor shifted with profit.

sentences.zh: 善诱学者，谆谆不倦。

translations.literal: Skilled at guiding learners, earnest and tireless.
translations.idiomatic: He guided students with tireless earnestness.

sentences.zh: 临川吴澄，尝称栎有功于硃氏为多，凡江东人来受业于澄者，尽遣而归栎。

translations.literal: Wu Cheng of Linchuan once said that Li's service to the Zhu school was especially great; whenever anyone from east of the Yangzi came to study with Cheng, he sent them all back to study with Li.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng of Linchuan said Li had done more for the Zhu school than anyone else, and sent every student from east of the Yangzi who came to him back to study with Li instead.

sentences.zh: 栎所居堂曰定宇，学者因以定宇先生称之。

translations.literal: The hall where Li dwelt was called Dingyu, and scholars therefore called him Master Dingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His hall was called Dingyu, and scholars called him Master Dingyu.

sentences.zh: 元统二年卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yuantong at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 揭傒斯志其墓，乃与吴澄并称，曰：「澄居通都大邑，又数登用于朝，天下学者，四面而归之，故其道远而章，尊而明。

translations.literal: Jie Xisi wrote his tomb inscription and paired him with Wu Cheng, saying: "Cheng dwelt in great communicating cities and was repeatedly employed at court; scholars throughout the realm converged upon him from the four sides, and therefore his Way was far-reaching and manifest, honored and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xisi wrote his tomb inscription and compared him with Wu Cheng: "Cheng lived in great cities, served repeatedly at court, and drew scholars from every quarter. His Way was therefore far-reaching, honored, and bright.

sentences.zh: 栎居万山间，与木石俱，而足迹未尝出乡里，故其学必待其书之行，天下乃能知之。

translations.literal: Li dwelt among ten thousand mountains, together with trees and stones, and his footsteps never left his home district; therefore his learning had to await the circulation of his books before the realm could know it.
translations.idiomatic: Li lived among ten thousand mountains with only trees and stone for company and never left his home district. The world could know his learning only when his books circulated.

sentences.zh: 及其行也，亦莫之御，是可谓豪杰之士矣。」

translations.literal: Yet once they circulated, none could withstand them—this may be called a heroic scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Yet once they appeared, nothing could stop them. He was truly a man of heroic stature."

sentences.zh: 世以为知言。

translations.literal: The age considered this discerning speech.
translations.idiomatic: The age judged this a penetrating verdict.

sentences.zh: 胡一桂，字庭芳，徽州婺源人。

translations.literal: Hu Yigui, courtesy name Tingfang, was a native of Wuyuan in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yigui, styled Tingfang, came from Wuyuan in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 父方平。

translations.literal: His father was Fangping.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Fangping.

sentences.zh: 一桂生而颖悟，好读书，尤精于《易》。

translations.literal: Yigui was intelligent from birth, loved reading, and was especially accomplished in the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui was clever from childhood, loved books, and was especially accomplished in the Changes.

sentences.zh: 初，饶州德兴沈贵宝，受《易》于董梦程，梦程受硃熹之《易》黄ＯＥ，而一桂之父方平及从贵宝、梦程学，尝著《易学启蒙通释》。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shen Guibao of Dexing in Raozhou received the Changes from Dong Mengcheng; Mengcheng received Zhu Xi's Changes from Huang Gan, and Yigui's father Fangping had followed Guibao and Mengcheng in study and once composed Comprehensive Explanation of the Introduction to the Study of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guibao of Dexing in Raozhou had studied the Changes under Dong Mengcheng, who had received Zhu Xi's teaching from Huang Gan. Yigui's father Fangping studied with Guibao and Mengcheng and wrote Comprehensive Explanation of the Introduction to the Study of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 一桂之学，出于方平，得硃熹氏源委之正。

translations.literal: Yigui's learning issued from Fangping and obtained the correct lineage of the Zhu school from source to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Yigui's learning came through Fangping and preserved the authentic Zhu Xi lineage.

sentences.zh: 宋景定甲子，一桂年十八，遂领乡荐，试礼部不敏，退而讲学，远近师之，号双湖先生。

translations.literal: In the jiazi year of Song's Jingding era, when Yigui was eighteen, he received provincial recommendation; he tested at the Ministry of Rites without success, withdrew and lectured, and near and far took him as teacher, styling him Master Twin Lakes.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiazi year of Jingding, when he was eighteen, Yigui passed the provincial examination but failed at the Ministry of Rites. He withdrew to teach, and students came from far and near, calling him Master Twin Lakes.

sentences.zh: 所著书有《周易本义附录纂疏》、《本义启蒙翼传》、《硃子诗传附录纂疏》、《十七史纂》，并行于世。

translations.literal: Books he authored include Collated Commentary on the Appendix to the Original Meaning of the Zhou Changes, Winged Transmission of the Introduction to the Original Meaning, Collated Commentary on the Appendix to Zhu Xi's Commentary on the Odes, and Digest of the Seventeen Histories—all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Collated Commentary on the Appendix to the Original Meaning of the Changes, Winged Transmission of the Introduction to the Original Meaning, Collated Commentary on Zhu Xi's Odes, and Digest of the Seventeen Histories, all widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 其同郡胡炳文，字仲虎，亦以《易》名家，作《易本义通释》，而于硃熹所著《四书》，用力尤深。

translations.literal: Hu Bingwen of the same commandery, courtesy name Zhonghu, was also famed as a master of the Changes and composed Comprehensive Explanation of the Original Meaning of the Changes; in Zhu Xi's Four Books he applied effort especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bingwen of the same prefecture, styled Zhonghu, was also renowned for the Changes and wrote Comprehensive Explanation of the Original Meaning of the Changes, but devoted his deepest effort to Zhu Xi's Four Books.

sentences.zh: 餘干饶鲁之学，本出于硃熹，而其为说，多与熹牴牾，炳文深正其非，作《四书通》，凡辞异而理同者，合而一之；

translations.literal: Rao Lu of Yugan—his learning originally issued from Zhu Xi, yet his doctrines often clashed with Xi. Bingwen deeply corrected his errors and composed Comprehensive Guide to the Four Books: wherever the wording differed but the principle was the same, he united them as one;
translations.idiomatic: Rao Lu of Yugan had studied Zhu Xi but often contradicted him. Bingwen corrected these errors in Comprehensive Guide to the Four Books, uniting passages that differed in wording but agreed in principle;

sentences.zh: 辞同而指异者，析而辨之，往往发其未尽之蕴。

translations.literal: where the wording was the same but the intent differed, he analyzed and distinguished them, often bringing forth meanings not yet fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: and analyzing passages that looked alike but meant different things, often drawing out meanings his predecessors had left implicit.

sentences.zh: 东南学者，因其所自号，称云峰先生。

translations.literal: Southeastern scholars, according to the style name he gave himself, called him Master Cloud Peak.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern scholars called him Master Cloud Peak from the name he chose for himself.

sentences.zh: 炳文尝用荐者，署明经书院山长，再调兰溪州学正。

translations.literal: Bingwen was once employed through recommendation as head of the Mingjing Academy and was later transferred to be director of studies in Lanxi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through recommendation Bingwen served as head of the Mingjing Academy and later as director of studies in Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 黄泽，字楚望，其先长安人。

translations.literal: Huang Ze, courtesy name Chuwang, was by ancestry a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ze, styled Chuwang, came from a family originally of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 唐末，舒艺知资州内江县，卒，葬焉，子孙遂为资州人。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, Shu Yi governed Neijiang county in Zizhou, died, and was buried there; his descendants thus became natives of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tang, Shu Yi governed Neijiang in Zizhou, died there, and was buried there; his descendants became natives of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，延节为大理评事，兼监察御史，累赠金紫光禄大夫，泽十一世祖也。

translations.literal: Early in Song, Yanjie was an evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and concurrently a surveillance censor; he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon—Ze's eleventh-generation ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song his ancestor Yanjie served as judicial reviewer and surveillance censor and was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon—Ze's eleventh-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 五世祖拂，与二兄播、揆，同年登进士第，蜀人荣之。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Fu, together with his two elder brothers Bo and Kui, passed the jinshi examination in the same year—a glory for the people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Fu and his elder brothers Bo and Kui all passed the jinshi in the same year, a glory for Shu.

sentences.zh: 父仪可，累举不第，随兄骥子官九江，蜀乱，不能归，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yike repeatedly took the examinations without success, followed his elder brother Jizi in office at Jiujiang; when Shu fell into turmoil he could not return and therefore made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yike failed the examinations repeatedly, followed his elder brother Jizi to an office at Jiujiang, and when Shu fell into chaos could not return home, settling there instead.

sentences.zh: 泽生有异质，慨然以明经学道为志，好为苦思，屡以成疾，疾止复思，久之，如有所见，作《颜渊仰高钻坚论》。

translations.literal: Ze was born with unusual gifts and resolutely took clarifying the classics and learning the Way as his aim. He loved strenuous thinking, often fell ill from it, and when illness ceased would think again; after long effort it was as though he had a vision, and he composed the Treatise on Yan Yuan Looking Up High and Drilling Hard.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was gifted from birth and resolved to master the classics and pursue the Way. He thought so hard he often fell ill; when he recovered he thought again. After long effort he seemed to see clearly and wrote On Yan Yuan Looking Upward and Drilling Deep.

sentences.zh: 蜀人治经，必先古注疏，泽于名物度数，考核精审，而义理一宗程、硃，作《易春秋二经解》、《二礼祭祀述略》。

translations.literal: Shu people in studying the classics always began with ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; Ze in names and objects, numbers and measures, examined and verified with precision, while in principle he took the Cheng and Zhu schools as sole authority, composing Exegesis of the Two Classics Changes and Spring and Autumn and Outline of Sacrificial Rites in the Two Ritual Books.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan scholars traditionally began with ancient commentaries. Ze examined names, measures, and numbers with meticulous care while taking Cheng–Zhu doctrine as his standard, and wrote Exegesis of the Changes and Spring and Autumn and Outline of Sacrificial Rites in the Two Ritual Books.

sentences.zh: 大德中，江西行省相臣闻其名，授江州景星书院山长，使食其禄以施教。

translations.literal: In the Dade era the chief minister of the Jiangxi Regional Secretariat heard his name and appointed him head of the Jingxing Academy in Jiangzhou, enabling him to receive stipend while teaching.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era the Jiangxi regional chief minister appointed him head of the Jingxing Academy in Jiangzhou on salary so he could teach.

sentences.zh: 又为山长于洪之东湖书院，受学者益众。

translations.literal: He also served as head of the East Lake Academy in Hong, and those who received instruction from him grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He later headed the East Lake Academy in Hong, and his following grew still larger.

sentences.zh: 始泽尝梦见夫子，以为适然，既而屡梦见之，最后乃梦夫子手授所较《六经》，字画如新，由是深有感发，始悟所解经多徇旧说为非是，乃作《思古吟》十章，极言圣人德容之盛，上达于文王、周公。

translations.literal: At first Ze once dreamed of the Master and thought it accidental; then he dreamed of him repeatedly, and finally dreamed that the Master handed him in person the collated Six Classics, their characters fresh as new. From this he was deeply moved and awakened, and first understood that much of his exegesis of the classics had followed old doctrines in error. He therefore composed ten chapters of Chants of Thinking on Antiquity, expounding to the utmost the sage's virtue and bearing, reaching up to King Wen and the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ze first dreamed of Confucius by chance, then dreamed of him again and again, and at last dreamed that Confucius handed him a freshly collated set of the Six Classics. Deeply moved, he realized how much of his earlier exegesis had merely followed old errors. He wrote ten Chants of Thinking on Antiquity celebrating the sage's virtue and bearing up to King Wen and the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 秩满即归，闭门授徒以养亲，不复言仕。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he returned at once, closed his doors to teach disciples and support his parents, and spoke of office no more.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he went home, closed his doors to teach and support his parents, and never spoke of office again.

sentences.zh: 尝以为去圣久远，经籍残阙，传注家率多傅会，近世儒者，又各以才识求之，故议论虽多，而经旨愈晦；

translations.literal: He once considered that distant from the sages for so long, the classics were damaged and deficient; commentators mostly forced interpretations, and recent Confucians each sought the meaning through personal talent and insight—therefore although discussions were many, the purport of the classics grew ever more obscure;
translations.idiomatic: He believed that with the sages so far in the past and the texts damaged, commentators mostly forced their readings while modern scholars relied on personal cleverness, so debate multiplied even as the classics' meaning grew obscurer;

sentences.zh: 必积诚研精，有所悟入，然后可以窥见圣人之本真。

translations.literal: one must accumulate sincerity and study with refinement, have some awakening and entry, and only then can one glimpse the sages' authentic reality.
translations.idiomatic: only through accumulated sincerity and refined study, with genuine insight, can one glimpse the sages' authentic teaching.

sentences.zh: 乃揭《六经》中疑义千有餘条，以示学者。

translations.literal: He therefore set forth more than a thousand doubtful points in the Six Classics to show learners.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore listed more than a thousand doubtful points in the Six Classics for his students.

sentences.zh: 既乃尽悟失传之旨。

translations.literal: Thereafter he fully awakened to meanings that had been lost in transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he fully grasped meanings long lost in transmission.

sentences.zh: 自言每于幽闲寂寞、颠沛流离、疾病无聊之际得之，及其久也，则豁然无不贯通。

translations.literal: He said himself that he obtained understanding especially in moments of secluded quiet, loneliness, displacement and wandering, illness and boredom; when this had lasted long, everything suddenly opened and nothing failed to connect through.
translations.idiomatic: He said insight came especially in solitude, exile, sickness, and idleness; sustained over time, everything suddenly opened and connected.

sentences.zh: 自天地定位、人物未生已前，沿而下之，凡邃古之初，万化之原，载籍所不能具者，皆昭若发蒙，如示诸掌。

translations.literal: From the fixing of Heaven and Earth and before the birth of human beings, tracing downward—all the depths of remote antiquity, the origins of the myriad transformations that written records cannot fully contain—became bright as if lifting blindness, as if shown upon the palm.
translations.idiomatic: From the ordering of Heaven and Earth down through ages before humanity, every remote origin and source of transformation that books could not fully record became clear as daylight, plain as the palm of his hand.

sentences.zh: 然后由伏羲、神农、五帝、三王，以及春秋之末，皆若身在其间，而目击其事者。

translations.literal: Then from Fuxi, Shennong, the Five Emperors, and the Three Kings down to the end of the Spring and Autumn—it was all as if he were personally present among them, witnessing events with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi and Shennong through the Five Emperors and Three Kings to the end of the Spring and Autumn era, it was as if he had been present and witnessed every event himself.

sentences.zh: 于是《易》、《春秋》传注之失，《诗》、《书》未决之疑，《周礼》非圣人书之谤，凡数十年苦思而未通者，皆涣然冰释，各就条理。

translations.literal: Thereupon errors in the commentaries on the Changes and Spring and Autumn, unresolved doubts in the Odes and Documents, the slander that the Rites of Zhou was not the sage's book—all that he had thought on bitterly for decades without penetrating suddenly melted like ice and each found its proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in commentaries on the Changes and Spring and Autumn, unresolved doubts in the Odes and Documents, the claim that the Rites of Zhou was not authentic—all puzzles he had wrestled with for decades melted away and fell into order.

sentences.zh: 故于《易》以明象为先，以因孔子之言，上求文王、周公之意为主，而其机括，则尽在《十翼》，作《十翼举要》、《忘象辩》、《象略》、《辩同论》。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Changes he took clarifying the images as foremost, and through Confucius' words sought upward primarily the intent of King Wen and the Duke of Zhou, while the pivot lay entirely in the Ten Wings. He composed Essentials of the Ten Wings, Discourse on Forgetting the Images, Outline of the Images, and Discourse on Distinguishing Sameness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changes he began with the images, used Confucius' words to recover King Wen and the Duke of Zhou, and treated the Ten Wings as the key. He wrote Essentials of the Ten Wings, On Forgetting the Images, Outline of the Images, and On Distinguishing Sameness.

sentences.zh: 于《春秋》以明书法为主，其大要则在考核三传，以求向上之功，而脉络尽在《左传》，作《三传义例考》、《笔削本旨》。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn he took clarifying the brush method as primary; the great essentials lay in examining the Three Commentaries to seek the upward achievement, while the thread ran entirely through the Zuo Commentary. He composed Examination of the Principles and Examples of the Three Commentaries and Original Aim of the Brush Editing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn he focused on the Annals' brush method, tested the Three Commentaries to recover the original intent, and treated the Zuo Commentary as the thread. He wrote Examination of the Principles of the Three Commentaries and Original Aim of the Brush Editing.

sentences.zh: 又作《元年春王正月辩》、《诸侯娶女立子通考》、《鲁隐公不书即位义》、《殷周诸侯禘祫考》、《周庙太庙单祭合食说》，作《丘甲辩》，凡如是者十餘通，以明古今礼俗不同，见虚辞说经之无益。

translations.literal: He also composed Discourse on "In the first year, spring, the king's first month," Comprehensive Examination of Lords Taking Wives and Establishing Sons, Meaning of Duke Yin's Not Recording Accession to the Throne, Examination of Di and Xia Sacrifices among Lords of Yin and Zhou, and Discourse on Separate and Combined Sacrificial Feasts in the Zhou Ancestral Temple and Grand Temple, and Discourse on the Hillock Jia—more than ten such works in all—to show that ritual and custom differ between past and present and to reveal the uselessness of empty words in explaining the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote more than ten works including On "The King's First Month of Spring in the First Year," Comprehensive Examination of Lords' Marriages and Heirs, Why Duke Yin Did Not Record His Accession, Di and Xia Sacrifices in Yin and Zhou, and Separate and Combined Temple Feasts, plus On the Hillock Jia, to show how ritual differed across ages and how empty commentary on the classics availed nothing.

sentences.zh: 尝言：「学者必悟经旨废失之由，然后圣人本意可见，若《易象》与《春秋》书法废失大略相似，苟通其一，则可触机而悟矣。」
