translations.literal: He once said: "The learner must understand the reasons why the purport of the classics was lost and abandoned; only then can the sages' original intent be seen. The loss of the images in the Changes and the brush method in the Spring and Autumn are broadly similar—if one penetrates either, one can touch the trigger and awaken to the other."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Students must grasp why the classics' meaning was lost before the sages' intent can reappear. The loss of the Changes' images and the Spring and Autumn's brush method are much alike: master one and you can awaken to the other by analogy."

sentences.zh: 又惧学者得于创闻，不复致思，故所著多引而不发，乃作《易学滥觞》、《春秋指要》，示人以求端用力之方。

translations.literal: He also feared that learners, obtaining something from a fresh hearing, would not think further; therefore in what he authored he mostly cited without unfolding. He then composed Sources of the Study of the Changes and Essentials of the Spring and Autumn to show people the methods of seeking the root and applying effort.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing students would stop thinking after a first hearing, he often cited without fully expounding. He therefore wrote Sources of the Study of the Changes and Essentials of the Spring and Autumn to show how to find one's footing and apply effort.

sentences.zh: 其于礼学，则谓郑氏深而未完，王肃明而实浅，作《礼经复古正言》。

translations.literal: Regarding ritual learning, he said that Master Zheng was deep yet not complete, and Wang Su was clear yet in fact shallow; he composed Correct Words on Restoring Antiquity in the Rites Classic.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual studies he held that Zheng Xuan went deep but left gaps, while Wang Su seemed clear but was actually shallow, and wrote Correct Words on Restoring Antiquity in the Rites Classic.

sentences.zh: 如王肃混郊丘废五天帝，并昆仑、神州为一，赵伯循言王者禘其始祖之所自出，以始祖配之，而不及群庙之社，胡宏家学不信《周礼》，以社为祭地之类，皆引经以证其非。

translations.literal: Such as Wang Su mixing suburban and mount-qi sacrifices and abolishing the five Heavenly Emperors, merging Kunlun and Spirit Province into one; Zhao Boxun saying that the king in di sacrifice honors the ultimate ancestor from whom the lineage springs and matches the ultimate ancestor, yet not extending to the altars of earth in the mass of temples; Hu Hong's family learning not believing the Rites of Zhou, treating she as sacrifice to earth and the like—all cited the classics to prove their errors.
translations.idiomatic: He took on errors such as Wang Su's conflation of suburban and mount-qi rites and abolition of the five Heavenly Emperors, or merging Kunlun and Spirit Province into one; Zhao Boxun's claim that the king's di sacrifice honors only the lineage's founding ancestor without reaching the communal temple altars of earth; and Hu Hong's family school, which rejected the Rites of Zhou and treated she as mere sacrifice to the earth—all proved wrong by appeal to the classics.

sentences.zh: 其辩释诸经要旨，则有《六经补注》；

translations.literal: For elucidating the essential purport of the various classics, there is Supplementary Notes on the Six Classics;
translations.idiomatic: To clarify the essentials of the classics he wrote Supplementary Notes on the Six Classics;

sentences.zh: 诋排百家异义，则取杜牧不当言而言之义，作《翼经罪言》。

translations.literal: to rebut the divergent doctrines of the hundred schools, he took Du Mu's meaning of speaking what ought not to be spoken and composed Wings to the Classics: Words of Blame.
translations.idiomatic: to refute rival schools he drew on Du Mu's insight about saying what should not be said and wrote Wings to the Classics: Words of Blame.

sentences.zh: 近代覃思之学，推泽为第一。

translations.literal: In recent learning of profound reflection, Ze was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among scholars of his day who thought deeply, Ze was held first.

sentences.zh: 吴澄尝观其书，以为平生所见明经士，未有能及之者，谓人曰：「能言距杨、墨者，圣人之徒也，楚望真其人乎！」

translations.literal: Wu Cheng once read his books and thought that among classicists he had seen in his life, none could match him; he said to people: "Those who can speak and keep distance from Yang and Mo are disciples of the sages—is Chuwang truly such a person?!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng read his works and declared that in a lifetime among experts on the classics he had never met his equal. He said, "Those who can argue against Yangism and Mohism are true followers of the sages—is Chuwang really such a man?"

sentences.zh: 然泽雅自慎重，未尝轻与人言。

translations.literal: Yet Ze was elegant and self-restrained and never lightly spoke with others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ze was reserved by nature and rarely spoke freely with anyone.

sentences.zh: 李泂使过九江，请北面称弟子，受一经，且将经纪其家，泽谢曰：「以君之才，何经不可明，然亦不过笔授其义而已。

translations.literal: Li Tong, passing through Jiujiang as an envoy, asked to face north and call himself a disciple, receive one classic, and was about to manage his household affairs; Ze declined, saying: "With your talent, what classic could not be clarified? Yet that too would only be passing its meaning by brush.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy Li Tong passed Jiujiang he asked to face north as a disciple, study one classic, and even manage Ze's household. Ze refused: "With your gifts any classic could be mastered—but that would only mean copying its meaning onto paper.

sentences.zh: 若餘则于艰苦之餘，乃能有见，吾非邵子，不敢以二十年林下期君也。」

translations.literal: As for me, only after hardship can there be insight; I am not Master Shao—I dare not pledge twenty years with you in the forest."
translations.idiomatic: As for me, insight comes only after hardship. I am no Master Shao, and I dare not bind you to twenty years in the woods with me."

sentences.zh: 泂叹息而去。

translations.literal: Tong sighed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Tong sighed and left.

sentences.zh: 或问泽：「自閟如此，宁无不传之惧？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Ze: "Closing yourself off like this—surely you fear that nothing will be handed down?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Ze, "By shutting yourself away like this, do you not fear your learning will die with you?"

sentences.zh: 泽曰：「圣经兴废，上关天运，子以为区区人力所致耶！」

translations.literal: Ze said: "The rise and fall of the sages' classics concerns heavenly fate above—do you think petty human effort caused it?!"
translations.idiomatic: Ze replied, "Whether the sacred classics flourish or perish hangs on heaven's decree—do you imagine mere human effort could decide that?!"

sentences.zh: 泽家甚窭贫，且年老，不复能教授，经岁大侵，家人采木实草根以疗饥，晏然曾不动其意，惟以圣人之心不明，而经学失传，若己有罪为大戚。

translations.literal: Ze's family was very poor, and he was old and could no longer teach; year after year there was great famine, and the household gathered tree fruit and grass roots to stave off hunger. He remained calm and never shifted his intent, grieving only that the sages' hearts were not clear and classical learning was lost—as if he himself were greatly at fault.
translations.idiomatic: His family was destitute and he too old to teach. Famine returned year after year; they lived on tree fruit and roots while he stayed unmoved, grieving only that the sages' intent was obscured and the classics lost—as though the fault were his alone.

sentences.zh: 至正六年卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Zhizheng, at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其书存于世者十二三。

translations.literal: Of his books, two or three tenths survive in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Only twenty or thirty percent of his writings survive.

sentences.zh: 门人惟新安赵汸为高第，得其《春秋》之学为多。

translations.literal: Among his disciples only Zhao Fang of Xin'an was a top graduate, receiving the most of his Spring and Autumn learning.
translations.idiomatic: Of his students only Zhao Fang of Xin'an ranked highest and inherited most of his Spring and Autumn scholarship.

sentences.zh: 萧渼，字惟斗，其先北海人。

translations.literal: Xiao Mian, styled Weidou, was by origin a man of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mian, styled Weidou, came from Beihai by ancestry.

sentences.zh: 父仕秦中，遂为奉元人。

translations.literal: His father served in the Qin region and thus became a man of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father took office in the Qin region, and the family became natives of Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 渼性至孝，自为兒时，翘楚不凡。

translations.literal: Mian's nature was utmost filial; from childhood he was outstanding beyond the common.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he stood out even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 稍出为府史，上官语不合，即引退，读书面山者三十年。

translations.literal: He briefly went out as a prefectural clerk; when his superior's words did not agree with his, he withdrew at once and faced the mountain in reading for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly served as a prefectural clerk, but when his superior's views clashed with his he resigned and read facing the hills for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 制一革衣，由身半以下，及卧，辄倚其榻，玩诵不少置，于是博极群书，天文、地理、律历、算数，靡不研究。

translations.literal: He made one leather garment from the waist down; when he lay down he always leaned it against his couch and recited without pause. Thus he mastered all books—astronomy, geography, calendrics, and mathematics—none of which he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a single leather coat from the waist down and, even in bed, propped it on his couch and kept reciting without rest until he had mastered every field—astronomy, geography, calendrics, and mathematics alike.

sentences.zh: 侯均谓元有天下百年，惟萧惟斗为识字人。

translations.literal: Hou Jun said that in the century since the Yuan possessed the realm, only Xiao Weidou was a literate man.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jun remarked that in a century under the Yuan, Xiao Weidou alone truly knew the written word.

sentences.zh: 学者及其门受业者甚众。

translations.literal: Scholars and those who received instruction at his gate were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Students and scholars who studied at his door were legion.

sentences.zh: 尝出，遇一妇人，失金钗道旁，疑渼拾之，谓曰：「殊无他人，独翁居后耳。」

translations.literal: Once when he went out he met a woman who had lost a gold hairpin by the roadside; she suspected Mian had picked it up and said, "Truly there is no one else—only you, elder, live behind here."
translations.idiomatic: Once abroad he met a woman who had lost a gold hairpin on the road. Suspecting he had taken it, she said, "There is no one else about—only you live back here, sir."

sentences.zh: 渼令随至门，取家钗以偿。

translations.literal: Mian had her follow him to his door and took a family hairpin to compensate her.
translations.idiomatic: He had her come to his house and gave her one of his family's hairpins in compensation.

sentences.zh: 其妇后得所遗钗，愧谢还之。

translations.literal: The woman later found the hairpin she had lost, apologized in shame, and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: She later recovered the lost pin, returned his in embarrassment, and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 乡人有自城中暮归者，遇寇，欲加害，诡言「我萧先生也」，寇惊愕释去。

translations.literal: A villager returning from the city at dusk met bandits who were about to harm him; he falsely said, "I am Master Xiao," and the bandits, startled, released him and left.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor returning from town at dusk was seized by robbers; he cried, "I am Master Xiao," and they, awed, let him go.

sentences.zh: 世祖分籓在秦，辟渼与杨恭懿、韩择侍秦邸，渼以疾辞，授陕西儒学提举，不赴。

translations.literal: When Shizu was enfeoffed in Qin he summoned Mian together with Yang Gongyi and Han Ze to attend the Qin residence; Mian declined on grounds of illness, was appointed Shaanxi Commissioner for Confucian Learning, and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai held his Qin fief he invited Mian, Yang Gongyi, and Han Ze to his household; Mian pleaded illness, was named Shaanxi Commissioner for Confucian Learning, and still refused.

sentences.zh: 省宪大臣即其家具宴为贺，使一从史先诣渼舍，渼方汲水灌园，从史至，不知其为渼也，使饮其马，即应之不拒，及冠带迎宾，从史见渼，有惧色，渼殊不为意。

translations.literal: A great minister of the provincial censorate took furniture to his home to give a feast in celebration and sent one attendant clerk ahead to Mian's dwelling. Mian was drawing water to irrigate the garden; when the clerk arrived he did not know it was Mian and had him water his horse. Mian complied without refusal. When he capped and girdled himself to welcome the guest, the clerk saw Mian and showed fear, but Mian was not concerned in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials prepared a celebratory feast at his home and sent a clerk ahead. Mian was watering his garden; the clerk, not recognizing him, ordered him to water his horse, and Mian obeyed without protest. When he dressed to receive the guests the clerk saw who he was and turned fearful, but Mian took no notice.

sentences.zh: 后累授集贤直学士、国子司业，改集贤侍读学士，皆不赴。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Vice Director of the National University, then changed to Attendant Academician—all of which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later posts as Direct Academician, National University Vice Director, and Attendant Academician followed; he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，拜太子右谕德，扶病至京师，入觐东宫，书《酒诰》为献，以朝廷时尚酒故也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade he was appointed Right Tutor of the Crown Prince; supporting himself through illness he reached the capital, had audience in the Eastern Palace, and presented the Wine Admonition in writing because the court at the time favored wine.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 11 he became Right Tutor to the Crown Prince. Ill but dutiful, he went to court, entered the Eastern Palace, and presented the Wine Admonition because drinking was fashionable at court.

sentences.zh: 寻以病力请去职，人问其故，则曰：「在礼，东宫东面，师傅西面，此礼今可行乎？」

translations.literal: Soon, pleading illness, he forcefully requested leave; when people asked the reason he said: "In ritual, the Eastern Palace faces east and the teacher faces west—can this ritual be carried out today?"
translations.idiomatic: He soon begged leave on grounds of illness. Asked why, he said, "Ritual requires the Eastern Palace to face east and the tutor west—can that still be observed?"

sentences.zh: 俄除集贤学士、国子祭酒，依前右谕德，疾作，固辞而归。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Academician and Libationer of the National University while retaining the right tutorship; when illness set in he firmly declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Academician and University Libationer while keeping the tutorship, but when illness worsened he refused firmly and went home.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十八，赐谥贞敏。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight; the posthumous title Zhenmin was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight and was posthumously titled Zhenmin.

sentences.zh: 渼制行甚高，真履实践，其教人，必自《小学》始。

translations.literal: Mian's conduct was very lofty and his practice genuine; in teaching people he always began from the Elementary Learning.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct was exalted and his practice sincere; he always began instruction with the Elementary Learning.

sentences.zh: 为文辞，立意精深，言近而指远，一以洙、泗为本，濂、洛、考亭为据，关辅之士，翕然宗之，称为一代醇儒。

translations.literal: In literary composition his intent was profound; his words were near yet pointed far—taking Zhu and Si as root and Lian, Luo, and Kaoting as basis. Scholars of Guanzhong all revered him and called him a pure Confucian of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His writing aimed deep: plain on the surface yet far-reaching in import, rooted in Confucius and Mencius and grounded in the Song masters from Lian and Luo to Kaoting. Guanzhong scholars revered him as the age's purest Confucian.

sentences.zh: 所著有《三礼说》、《小学标题驳论》、《九州志》，及《勤斋文集》，行于世。

translations.literal: What he authored includes Discourse on the Three Rites, Refutation of Titles in the Elementary Learning, Record of the Nine Provinces, and the Collected Works of the Diligent Studio, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works—Discourse on the Three Rites, Refutation of Titles in the Elementary Learning, Record of the Nine Provinces, and the Diligent Studio Collection—circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 韩择者，字从善，亦奉元人。

translations.literal: Han Ze, styled Congshan, was also a man of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze, styled Congshan, was likewise from Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 天资超异，信道不惑，其教学者，虽中岁以后，亦必使自《小学》等书始。

translations.literal: His natural endowment was surpassingly unusual; he believed in the Way without wavering. In teaching learners, even if they came after mid-life, he always made them begin from the Elementary Learning and such books.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and steadfast in the Way, he required every student—even latecomers—to start with the Elementary Learning and related texts.

sentences.zh: 或疑为陵节勤苦，则曰：「人不知学，白首童心，且童蒙所当知，而皓首不知，可乎？」

translations.literal: Some suspected this overstepped proper gradation and was laborious; he said: "If people do not know learning, they remain childlike in mind even with white hair—and what children should know, if white-haired men do not know, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: When some thought this too rigorous he replied, "Without learning one stays childish to the grave. What a child must know, should a gray-haired man remain ignorant?"

sentences.zh: 择尤邃礼学，有质问者，口讲指画无倦容。

translations.literal: Ze was especially profound in ritual learning; when questioners came he lectured with gestures and never showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in ritual studies and lectured tirelessly, illustrating every point with his hands.

sentences.zh: 士大夫游宦过秦中，必往见择，莫不虚往而实归焉。

translations.literal: Officials traveling through Qin on government business always went to see Ze, and none failed to return empty of expectation yet full of gain.
translations.idiomatic: Every official passing through Qin sought him out and left with more than they had hoped.

sentences.zh: 世祖尝召之赴京，疾，不果行。

translations.literal: Shizu once summoned him to the capital, but illness prevented the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once summoned him to court, but illness kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，门人为服缌麻者百餘人。

translations.literal: At his death more than a hundred disciples wore hemp mourning for him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death over a hundred disciples wore mourning hemp for him.

sentences.zh: 侯均者，字伯仁，亦奉元人。

translations.literal: Hou Jun, styled Boren, was also a man of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jun, styled Boren, was also from Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 父母蚤亡，独与继母居，卖薪以给奉养。

translations.literal: His parents died early; he lived alone with his stepmother and sold firewood to supply her support.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he lived with his stepmother and sold firewood to support her.

sentences.zh: 积学四十年，群经百氏，无不淹贯，旁通释、老外典。

translations.literal: He accumulated learning for forty years; of the classics and the hundred schools there was none he did not master thoroughly, and he also penetrated Buddhist and Daoist external texts.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years of study left him master of every classic and school, with deep knowledge of Buddhist and Daoist texts as well.

sentences.zh: 每读书，必熟诵乃已。

translations.literal: Whenever he read a book he had to recite it thoroughly before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: He would not set a book down until he had recited it through.

sentences.zh: 尝言：「人读书不至千遍，终于己无益。」

translations.literal: He once said: "If one does not read a text a thousand times, in the end it brings no benefit to oneself."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Unless you read a text a thousand times, it never truly becomes yours."

sentences.zh: 故其答诸生所问，穷索极探，如取诸箧笥。

translations.literal: Therefore in answering students' questions he probed to the utmost, as if taking things from a chest.
translations.idiomatic: His answers to students were exhaustive, as if drawn straight from a cabinet.

sentences.zh: 名振关中，学者宗之。

translations.literal: His fame shook Guanzhong, and scholars took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation filled Guanzhong, and scholars looked to him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 用荐者起为太常博士，后以上疏忤时相意，不待报可，即归休田里。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he was raised to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; later, because a memorial offended the chief minister, he did not wait for approval and at once returned to retire in his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended, he became Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite; when a memorial angered the chief minister he did not wait for dismissal but retired to his fields at once.

sentences.zh: 均貌魁梧，而气刚正，人多严惮之，及其应接之际，则和易款洽。

translations.literal: Jun's appearance was tall and imposing, his spirit stern and upright; many people stood in awe of him, yet when he received others he was gentle and cordial.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing, stern in bearing, he awed many—yet in conversation he was warm and easy.

sentences.zh: 虽方言古语，世所未晓者，莫不随问而答，世咸服其博闻。

translations.literal: Even dialect words and ancient speech the world had never understood—none failed to receive answers as asked; the world all submitted to his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Obscure dialects and archaic phrases none else understood he answered on the spot, and all marveled at his erudition.

sentences.zh: 恕之学，由程、硃上溯孔、孟，务贯浃事理，以利于行。

translations.literal: Shu's learning traced from Cheng and Zhu upward to Confucius and Mencius, striving to penetrate and saturate principle in things so as to benefit conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Shu's learning ran from Cheng and Zhu back to Confucius and Mencius, aiming to fuse principle with daily affairs so conduct would improve.

sentences.zh: 教人曲为开导，使得趣向之正。

translations.literal: In teaching people he bent every effort to guide them so they gained the correct orientation.
translations.idiomatic: He taught with patient, roundabout guidance until students found the right path.

sentences.zh: 性整洁，平居虽大暑，不去冠带。

translations.literal: His nature loved neatness; in ordinary life, even in great heat, he did not remove cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Fastidious by nature, he kept cap and sash even in midsummer heat.

sentences.zh: 母张夫人卒，事异母如事所生。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Zhang died, he served his stepmother as he would his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Zhang died he treated his stepmother exactly as his own mother.

sentences.zh: 父丧，哀毁致目疾，时祀斋肃详至。

translations.literal: At his father's death he was so grief-stricken that he damaged his eyes; in seasonal sacrifices he was reverent and thorough in detail.
translations.idiomatic: His father's death left him so grief-stricken that his sight failed; in ancestral rites he was meticulous to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 尝曰：「养生有不备，事犹可复，追远有不诚，是诬神也，可逭罪乎！」

translations.literal: He once said: "If nurturing the living is not fully provided for, the matter can still be remedied; if pursuit of the departed is not sincere, that is deceiving the spirits—can one escape guilt?!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Neglect while parents live can still be repaired; insincerity toward the dead deceives the spirits—how could guilt be avoided?"

sentences.zh: 与人交，虽外无适莫，而中有绳尺。

translations.literal: In dealings with others, though outwardly without favor or distance, inwardly he had a measuring standard.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he showed no favoritism, yet inwardly he held firm standards.

sentences.zh: 里人借骡而死，偿其直，不受，曰：「物之数也，何以偿为！」

translations.literal: A neighbor borrowed his mule and it died; he paid its value but would not accept it, saying: "It was the thing's allotted span—why compensate?!"
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's borrowed mule died he paid its worth but refused repayment, saying, "That was its fate—why take payment?"

sentences.zh: 家无儋石之储，而聚书数万卷，扁所居曰榘庵。

translations.literal: The household had no store of a dan and a shi, yet gathered tens of thousands of volumes of books; he inscribed his dwelling "Ju'an."
translations.idiomatic: Though he lacked even a modest grain store, he owned tens of thousands of books and named his house Ju'an, the Square Cottage.

sentences.zh: 时萧渼居南山下，亦以道高当世，入城府，必主恕家，士论称之曰「萧同」。

translations.literal: At the time Xiao Mian dwelt below the southern mountain, also esteemed in the Way for his age; entering the prefectural city he always lodged at Shu's home, and scholarly opinion called them "Xiao and Tong."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mian lived on the southern hills, likewise revered for his learning; whenever he entered town he stayed with Shu, and scholars paired them as "Xiao and Tong."

sentences.zh: 恕自京还，家居十三年，缙绅望之若景星麟凤，乡里称为先生而不姓。

translations.literal: After Shu returned from the capital he lived at home for thirteen years; gentry and officials looked to him as an auspicious star or qilin-phoenix, and villagers called him "Master" without his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Shu spent thirteen years at home after leaving the capital; officials regarded him as a rare treasure, and neighbors called him simply "the Master."

sentences.zh: 至顺二年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhishun at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 制赠翰林直学士，封京兆郡侯，谥文贞。

translations.literal: By decree he was posthumously made Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingzhao Commandery, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously named him Hanlin Direct Academician, Marquis of Jingzhao, with the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 其所著曰《榘庵集》，二十卷。

translations.literal: What he authored is called the Collected Works of Ju'an, in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works of Ju'an survives in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 恕弟子第五居仁，字士安，幼师萧渼，弱冠从恕受学。

translations.literal: Shu's disciple Di Wuju Ren, styled Shi'an, in youth studied under Xiao Mian; at twenty he received instruction from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Among Shu's disciples was Di Wuju Ren, styled Shi'an, who studied first with Xiao Mian and at twenty turned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 博通经史，躬率子弟致力农亩，而学徒满门。

translations.literal: He thoroughly mastered the classics and histories, personally led his sons and younger brothers in farming, yet his school was full of students.
translations.idiomatic: Master of classics and histories, he worked the fields with his sons and brothers while his school overflowed with students.

sentences.zh: 其宏度雅量，能容人所不能容。

translations.literal: His magnanimity and easy grace could accommodate what others could not.
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded, he tolerated what others could not bear.

sentences.zh: 尝行田间，遇有窃其桑者，居仁辄避之。

translations.literal: Once walking in the fields he met someone stealing his mulberries; Juren simply avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: Walking his fields one day he found a man stealing mulberries and simply turned aside.

sentences.zh: 乡里高其行义，率多化服。

translations.literal: The village esteemed his conduct and righteousness, and most were transformed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors honored his example, and many reformed their ways.

sentences.zh: 作字必楷整，游其门者，不惟学明，而行加修焉。

translations.literal: In writing characters he always used regular script; those who studied at his gate not only clarified learning but also improved their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote only in regular script, and students at his door improved in learning and in conduct alike.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，门人相与议易名之礼，私谥之曰静安先生。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his disciples together discussed the rite of changing the posthumous name and privately titled him Master Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his students debated his posthumous style and privately honored him as Master Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 安熙，字敬仲，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: An Xi, styled Jingzhong, was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: An Xi, styled Jingzhong, came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 祖滔，父松，皆以学行淑其乡人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tao and father Song both by learning and conduct made their village harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao and father Song were both learned and virtuous, bringing honor to their community.

sentences.zh: 熙既承其家学，及闻保定刘因之学，心向慕焉。

translations.literal: Xi inherited the family learning, and when he heard of the learning of Liu Yin of Baoding his heart turned toward it in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Xi inherited his family's scholarship and, hearing of Liu Yin of Baoding, yearned to study with him.

sentences.zh: 熙家与因所居相去数百里，因亦闻熙力于为已之学，深许与之。

translations.literal: Xi's home and where Yin dwelt were several hundred li apart; Yin also heard that Xi strove in learning for self-cultivation and deeply approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: They lived hundreds of li apart, yet Yin had heard of Xi's devoted self-cultivation and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 熙方将造其门，而因己殁，乃从因门人乌叔备问其绪说。

translations.literal: Xi was about to visit his door when Yin had already died; he therefore followed Yin's disciple Wu Shubei to inquire into his transmitted doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Xi set out to visit him, but Yin had already died; he then studied Liu's teachings with Wu Shubei, a disciple of Yin.

sentences.zh: 盖自因得宋儒硃熹之书，即尊信力行之，故其教人，必尊硃氏。

translations.literal: From Yin he obtained the books of the Song Confucian Zhu Xi and at once honored and practiced them with effort; therefore in teaching people he always took Master Zhu as authoritative.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yin's line he received Zhu Xi's works, revered them, and put them into practice, so his teaching always took Zhu as the standard.

sentences.zh: 然因之为人，高明坚勇，其进莫遏。

translations.literal: Yet Yin's person was lofty, firm, and brave; his advance could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin himself had been lofty, resolute, and fearless, pressing forward without restraint.

sentences.zh: 熙则简靓和易，务为下学之功。

translations.literal: Xi was simple, dignified, and easy-going, devoting himself to the work of elementary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was modest, serene, and approachable, stressing the foundations of learning.

sentences.zh: 其《告先圣文》有曰：「追忆旧闻，卒究前业。

translations.literal: His Address to the Former Sage says: "Recalling what I once heard, I finally exhaust the former enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: His Address to the Former Sage reads, "Recalling what I once heard, I carry on the work of those before.

sentences.zh: 洒扫应对，谨行信言。

translations.literal: Sweeping and responding, reverent conduct and trustworthy speech.
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping floors and answering questions, acting with reverence and speaking with integrity.

sentences.zh: 餘力学文，穷理尽性。

translations.literal: With remaining strength studying literature, exhausting principle and fulfilling nature.
translations.idiomatic: With spare strength I study texts, probing principle to fulfill human nature.

sentences.zh: 循循有序，发轫圣途，以存诸心，以行诸己，以及于物，以化于乡。」

translations.literal: Step by step in order, setting out on the sage's path—to preserve it in the heart, practice it in oneself, extend it to things, and transform the village."
translations.idiomatic: Step by step I advance on the sage's road—keeping it in the heart, living it in the self, reaching outward to things, and transforming the countryside."

sentences.zh: 其用功平实切密，可谓善学硃氏者。

translations.literal: His application of effort was level, solid, and close-grained—he can be called one who studied Zhu well.
translations.idiomatic: His effort was steady, practical, and meticulous—a true follower of Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙遭时承平，不屑仕进，家居教授垂数十年，四方之来学者，多所成就。

translations.literal: Xi encountered a time of peace and disdained seeking office; he taught at home for nearly several decades, and learners who came from the four directions mostly achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: Living in peaceful times he scorned office and taught at home for decades; students came from every quarter and many distinguished themselves.

sentences.zh: 既殁，乡人为立祠于藁城之西筦镇。

translations.literal: After his death the villagers erected a shrine for him west of Gaocheng at Xiguan Town.
translations.idiomatic: After his death locals built him a shrine west of Gaocheng at Xiguan Town.

sentences.zh: 其门人苏天爵，为辑其遗文，而虞集序之曰：「使熙得见刘氏，廓之以高明，厉之以奋发，则刘氏之学，当益昌大于时矣。」

translations.literal: His disciple Su Tianjue compiled his surviving writings, and Yu Ji prefaced them, saying: "If Xi had been able to see Master Liu, and Liu had broadened him with loftiness and spurred him with vigor, then Liu's learning would have flourished still greater in the age."
translations.idiomatic: His student Su Tianjue collected his remaining writings; Yu Ji wrote the preface: "Had Xi met Liu Yin, and Liu enlarged him with loftiness and urged him with vigor, Liu's school would have spread even wider in their time."
